published_implementation.historical_relation: The full first-party framework implements the agent communication, lease, policy and arbitration paths, while the published Scene 2 evaluation supplies a benchmark-authored conflict stimulus and scripted conflict/timeline messages around those implementation paths.

observations.scenario: A scheduled evening wind-down routine requests device-state changes while a user-explicit work-from-home mode remains active. The scene supplies conflicting lease requests and a conflict/timeline stimulus, then invokes the public framework arbitration and lease-evaluation paths before recording denials, acknowledgements and a resolution broadcast.
implementation_paths_exercised: Git-backed event persistence and timeline context
lease denial, agent acknowledgement and resolution broadcast
scaffolded_surface: the conflicting lease requests are authored by the Scene 2 script
the Dewey conflict alert is authored by the Scene 2 script
the timeline response used by arbitration is authored by the Scene 2 script
observations.result_summary: The first-party framework README reports that all five repeated Scene 2 runs detected and resolved the published conflict scenario.
observations.notes: The repository publishes aggregate repeated-run results and a deterministic metrics script but not a committed per-run result ledger for the five evaluation runs. A separate first-party demo repository includes a pre-recorded physical-deployment trace, but this observation does not equate that trace with the five aggregate evaluation runs.
